The student was attending a catered formal dinner at the University of Hong Kong and had to choose meal courses in advance, as part of accepting a place at the event. The word "courses" refers to meal courses, not academic classes, and the student did intend to eat the food themselves. However, when a course was served to the student at the dinner, the student sent it back to the kitchen. The returned dish was not replaced; instead, the caterer discarded it. Thus, by the end of that evening, all of the student's chosen courses had effectively vanished: they had been selected beforehand, rejected when served, and thrown away rather than eaten.
